verdict.rationale: Cal.com documents an open API (auth via key/OAuth) and an MIT-licensed self-host fork (Cal.diy) that could in principle let a user pull out their data and run independently, but there is no explicit 'export all my data' feature documented, and hands-on community reports directly contradict the openness/exit narrative: users say self-hosting the API isn't really possible ('there's no way to self-host the API... AGPL is a very restrictive license'), and more recent reports describe a bait-and-switch where Cal.diy/self-hosted docker images were pulled back and restricted to 'personal, non-production use,' with users abandoning self-hosting as a result. missing for 10: a documented data-export/portability feature, and confirmation that self-hosting reliably preserves full data ownership without restriction.
